title: External-validity probe with compressed reconstruction and strided arithmetic
question: Does the horizon-dependent KEEP_WARM versus FAULT_IN price-boundary ordering survive when the cold representation is gzip-compressed, runtime capability state is reconstructed into anonymous mmap, and semantic work uses strided arithmetic instead of the P9-011 hashing proxy?
preregistered_gates: all high-quota runs complete without kernel OOM
workspace and semantic signatures match across modes and repetitions at each horizon
compressed source is less than one sixteenth of runtime capability bytes
FAULT_IN reduces kernel memory peak by at least 8 MiB at horizons 2,4,8
FAULT_IN has higher total reconstruction time than KEEP_WARM at horizons 2,4,8
the derived break-even external RAM price rises monotonically over horizons 2,4,8
authority and retry authority remain unchanged
